prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1044; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed first notice of loss. Insured reports vehicle struck while turning left at an intersection. Other driver reportedly failed to yield on oncoming through lane. Both vehicles drivable from scene. Assigned file to field appraiser for vehicle inspection.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant states neck and back strain since the collision and has been seeking outpatient care. Claimant is not represented by counsel at this time. Explained claim process, requested medical records and authorization forms. Claimant agreed to send documents by mail.

Entry 3: Received police report. Report notes both drivers gave conflicting accounts of signal phase at the intersection. Witness statement on file supports claimant's version that insured had initiated the left turn on a green arrow. Liability assessment under review pending appraisal photos.

Entry 4: Appraisal completed on claimant vehicle. Rear bumper and quarter panel damage consistent with impact described. Repair estimate received from shop and under review. Medical authorization returned by claimant and submitted to records request. Initial treatment notes reflect diagnosis of cervical and lumbar strain with prescribed physical therapy.

Entry 5: Followed up with claimant regarding treatment status. Claimant reports ongoing stiffness but improving with therapy. Advised claimant of right to seek independent legal advice given injury component, and provided information on how to contact the claims department with questions. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect injury exposure. File remains open pending receipt of final therapy records.
